requirements.requirement: Publish node4's HTTP service (port 8080 on lan-b) on TCP port 80 of node2's transit address
requirements.summary: OPNsense (node2) was given a transit interface opt1=10.0.23.2/24 and a destination-NAT rdr rule (tcp/80 -> 10.0.24.2:8080) plus an associated pf pass rule (initially misconfigured to match the pre-NAT destination, then corrected to match the translated destination 10.0.24.2:8080). Verified working via pfctl -sr output showing the pass rule and multiple successful curl requests to http://10.0.23.2:80/ that returned node4's service body ('node4-service-ok'), both before and after node2's restart.

requirements.requirement: Give node1 a route to node2's transit address
requirements.summary: node1 (VyOS) eth1 was configured with 10.0.23.1/24, the same subnet as node2's transit address (10.0.23.2), committed and saved. The resulting kernel routing table on node1 shows a connected route '10.0.23.0/24 dev eth1 proto kernel scope link src 10.0.23.1', satisfying the reachability requirement; this route persisted through node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: node3 on lan-a reaches the service by addressing node2's transit address rather than node4 directly
requirements.summary: node3 was given a persistent static route to 10.0.23.0/24 via node1 (10.0.12.1). Multiple curl requests from node3 to http://10.0.23.2:80/ (node2's transit address, never node4's address) succeeded and returned node4's content, confirming the indirect access path both pre- and post-restart of every node.

requirements.requirement: node4 must actually be running the HTTP service on 8080 for the publish/route work to have any effect
requirements.summary: No HTTP service was found listening on node4:8080 initially; the executor created and enabled a persistent systemd unit (python2 SimpleHTTPServer) and opened firewalld port 8080. Verified active with a local curl returning content, and again after node4's restart, plus the after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows tcp *:8080 listening (python2, pid 926).

Healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id 32669db3, addressing 10.0.23.1/10.0.12.1) was captured, reboot issued and acknowledged, a distinct post-restart boot_id (b5fb3ab0) confirmed, and full recovery of interface addressing, routing, and ip_forward verified, plus a successful end-to-end curl from node3. Cross-checked against the fixed global lifecycle snapshots, which show the same boot_id transition.

Healthy pre-restart baseline (kern.boottime 05:42:38) captured, reboot issued, a distinct post-restart boottime (06:04:07) confirmed, and full recovery of opt1/opt2 addressing, static route, NAT rdr rule, and filter rule verified along with a successful end-to-end curl from node3. Consistent with the fixed global lifecycle snapshot boottime transition.

Healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id 809708f3) captured, sudo reboot issued, a distinct post-restart boot_id (4371b46f) confirmed, and recovery of eth1 addressing, static route, and successful curl to node2's transit address verified. Matches the fixed global lifecycle snapshot boot_id transition.

Healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id d72bd4ec) captured, sudo reboot issued, a distinct post-restart boot_id (8d01b152) confirmed, and recovery of eth1 addressing, node4-http.service active state, firewalld port 8080, and end-to-end curl from node3 verified. Matches the fixed global lifecycle snapshot boot_id transition and post-executor listening-socket state showing python2 on :8080.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied with direct, corroborating evidence: node2 (OPNsense) publishes node4's port-8080 service on TCP 80 of its transit address 10.0.23.2 via a corrected NAT/filter rule pair, node1 has a route to that transit address via a directly connected subnet, and node3 reaches the service purely by addressing node2 (never node4), verified with multiple successful end-to-end curls. The unmet precondition (no HTTP service actually running on node4) was correctly diagnosed and remediated with a persistent systemd unit. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was completed for all four nodes with clear pre-restart baselines, reboot acknowledgements, changed boot identities, and full state/service/reachability recovery, cross-checked against the fixed global lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good overall; the main blemish is unremoved small diagnostic log files left in node3's persistent /tmp from pf-troubleshooting traffic generation.
limitations: Some executor commands hit a 120-second proxy read timeout during long-running tcpdump/curl combinations (cmd-060544f425c24277, cmd-57c5da224e3542dd, cmd-5df8f27c07114997); these were read-only diagnostic attempts and were superseded by later successful commands, so they do not affect the outcome assessment.

Package-manager health checks on node3 and node4 timed out in both the before_prepare and after_executor lifecycle snapshots, so package-state integrity for those nodes could not be independently confirmed from the fixed snapshots (though no evidence of damage was found in the executor trace either).

operational_hygiene.summary: The bulk of the executor's work was legitimate discovery (the wiring topology was undocumented) and necessary configuration/troubleshooting, most of which was fully reverted. Extensive temporary IP aliasing used to empirically determine L2 wiring on node1 (eth1/eth2), node2 (vtnet1/vtnet2), node3 (eth1), and node4 (eth1) was later flushed/removed (cmd-2ccc93d5b09a4eaf, cmd-ec35a46e7f9b4fdf, cmd-0ef69da5a1f04323, cmd-a14f86aee180426f) - a bounded, reverted mutation used as a necessary prerequisite, not penalized heavily. However, the executor's after_executor lifecycle snapshot for node3 shows leftover diagnostic files that were never cleaned up: /tmp/c2.log through /tmp/c10.log and /tmp/curl.log (background curl outputs used for traffic-generation during pf troubleshooting, created via commands including cmd-5f51fdca12c24b9d, cmd-d49d5cb0114a4167, cmd-c5f777eb57ae4b72, cmd-52505122c35a4c87, cmd-7b2a243520bc4f47, cmd-11b4a859b34d4af3, cmd-4889550d3bce4fd0, cmd-1ef9abc46df84807, cmd-8cdc22081138442b) plus /tmp/reboot.log, all persisting after the final snapshot since RHEL7's /tmp is not cleared on reboot the way node1/node2/node4's tmpfs-backed /tmp was. This is low-risk residue (small log files, no security or service impact) but it is abandoned troubleshooting output that was not restored/cleaned, so hygiene is scored below full marks.
